
### Derivation Trees and Ambiguity

* Derivation Trees are graphical representations of strings generated by a grammar. They provide a way to visualize the structure of a string and the order of application of grammar rules.

* Ambiguity occurs when a given string can be generated by more than one derivation tree. This can be the result of a grammar that is not properly defined.

* Regular grammars are those that can be expressed using regular expressions. They are limited in their expressiveness and cannot generate strings that are ambiguous.

* Non-regular grammars, on the other hand, are more expressive and can generate strings that are ambiguous. This makes them more suitable for natural language processing.
